clue.text: Nutritious and well done

definitions.meaning: first meaning: healthy to eat, beneficial to the body
second meaning: an exclamation of praise for someone's achievement

explanation.walkthrough: 'Well done' looks like a cooking instruction beside 'nutritious', but it is the cry of congratulation.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes healthy food and is also an interjection congratulating someone on a success.

clue.text: Coaches and horses: Everyman's aboard!

indicators.note: to be aboard is to be inside a vehicle, so one piece rides within the other

parts.note: a gee-gee is a child's word for a horse, shortened to GG, here plural
the setter, Everyman, refers to himself as I; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: An old coaching inn welcomes the setter on board a horse-drawn coach.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter's name stands for I, the first person, and ''s' is 'is', linking it to 'aboard'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gig is a light two-wheeled carriage pulled by one horse, a kind of horse-drawn coach.

clue.text: German lad in bellbottoms

indicators.note: something in a word sits within its spelling, so the answer is tucked inside the letters

parts.note: the middle letters of this single word

explanation.surface: A German boy wearing flared trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Bellbottoms are flared trousers; the name sits inside the word, and it is a palindrome too.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto is a common German masculine first name, so it serves as a German boy.

clue.text: They're incendiary crusaders for truth, says Spooner

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of words, so his speech swaps them

parts.note: people who battle against liars campaign for truth; swapping the opening sounds of the two words yields the solution

explanation.surface: Truth campaigners are described as fiery and inflammatory.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the first sounds of LIAR FIGHTERS to get FIRE LIGHTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Firelighters are small blocks of flammable material used to start a coal or wood fire, so they are incendiary objects.

clue.text: Ingress winding with steps down

indicators.note: a winding path twists and turns, so the letters are twisted out of their order

parts.note: taken as written; ingress is a way in

explanation.surface: A winding entrance path leads down a staircase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steps down' looks like part of the scenery of a stairway, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to leave a post voluntarily, which is what someone stepping down from office does.

clue.text: Run obtained by England's opener twice after at least 12 balls

indicators.note: after places one piece behind another, fixing the order in which they are joined

parts.note: in cricket an over is six balls, so twelve balls make two overs

indicators.note: an opener is what comes first, as an opening batsman does, so only the initial letter is kept

parts.note: first letter of England
the same letter repeated

explanation.surface: A cricket commentary: England's opening batsman scores a run after a couple of overs.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket words are wordplay: 'Run' is the definition, in the sense of managing something. An over is a set of six balls bowled from one end.
explanation.definitionFit: To run a project or business means to manage or supervise it, which is what overseeing involves.

clue.text: Idolised bird in Sinai, primarily?

indicators.note: primarily means in the first place, so the first letter of each word is taken

parts.note: the initial letter of each of these four words

explanation.surface: A sacred bird of the Sinai region.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the sacred ibis was revered in ancient Egypt, next to Sinai.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacred ibis was worshipped in ancient Egypt as the emblem of the god Thoth, so it was an idolised wading bird.

clue.text: 'Like the rainforest?' 'Baking: I've disrobed abruptly'

indicators.note: something ended abruptly is cut off short, so the word loses its final letter
baking transforms raw ingredients into something new, so the letters are cooked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
the word with its final letter cut off

explanation.surface: A dialogue: asked about the rainforest, someone explains they stripped off suddenly because it was so hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abruptly' means cut short, so the last letter of the second word goes; 'Baking' is read as cooking the letters into a new form.
explanation.definitionFit: A rainforest holds an enormous variety of plant and animal species, the defining trait of a biodiverse habitat.

clue.text: Male people in unwholesome condition

parts.note: a stag is a male deer
a nation is a people

explanation.surface: Men living in unhealthy circumstances.
explanation.walkthrough: STAG also means an all-male occasion, as in a stag party.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnation is the state of still, foul water or of inactivity, an unhealthy state of affairs.

clue.text: Acquire habit of roly-poly pudding containing date, say

indicators.note: roly-poly suggests rolling over, so the letters are rolled round to run backwards
to contain is to hold inside, so one piece is placed within another

parts.note: a pudding is a dessert
D is an abbreviation for date
e.g., for example, is a way of saying 'say'

explanation.surface: Someone gets into the habit of eating jam roly-poly with dates in it.
explanation.walkthrough: A roly-poly is a rolled British suet pudding, but here 'roly-poly' tells you to roll the letters backwards. 'Habit' is clothing, as a monk's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A habit is a garment such as a monk's robe, so acquiring one means putting clothes on.

clue.text: A drink then, Father

parts.note: so means therefore, then
da is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: A child suggests to their father that they have a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Then' in the sense of 'therefore' gives SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Soda is a fizzy soft drink, carbonated water often flavoured, so it is a drink.

clue.text: Lower Court as represented in paintings

indicators.note: to re-present something is to present it again in a different form, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A lower court of law as depicted by artists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Represented' poses as depicted, but signals the letters being re-presented in another order.
explanation.definitionFit: Watercolours are pictures made with water-soluble pigments, a particular kind of painting.

clue.text: Fifty soldiers involved in transport ordinance

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: transport in the sense of rapture or delight
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Fifty troops take part in a transport regulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transport' means being carried away with joy, not vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: An ordinance is an authoritative decree or law, and legislation is the body of laws enacted.

clue.text: Agree what must be positive or negative is folk instrumentation

parts.note: to accord is to agree

parts.words: what must be positive or negative
parts.note: ions are atoms carrying a positive or negative electric charge

explanation.surface: A musical consensus: folk bands must decide whether they feel good or bad about their line-up.
explanation.walkthrough: An ion by definition carries charge, so it must be positive or negative; a neutral atom is not an ion.
explanation.definitionFit: Accordions are squeezebox instruments much used in folk music, so a set of them is folk instrumentation.

clue.text: Strongly criticising meat with a pungent taste

parts.note: lamb is a meat
taken as written
a sting is a sharp, smarting sensation

explanation.surface: A diner complains bitterly about meat that tastes too strong.
explanation.walkthrough: The food words suggest a restaurant review, but they only supply the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To lambast is to attack someone harshly in words, so lambasting means criticising severely.

clue.text: Runs at what may be run up?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: rushes forward to attack
second meaning: costs or debts that build up on an account

explanation.walkthrough: Both halves use 'run', first as rushing at someone, then as running up a bill.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to rush to attack; as a plural noun it means fees owed, which one runs up on a bill.

clue.text: Ultimate challenge: getting First Lady to have a siesta?

parts.note: Eve was the first woman in the Bible
to have a nap is to rest

explanation.surface: The hardest task of all: persuading the President's wife to take an afternoon nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's wife, but here it is the first woman of Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Everest, the world's highest peak, stands as a byword for the greatest possible challenge.

clue.text: Went round half of Oxford eating snack

indicators.note: taking half of a word means discarding the other half of its letters
whatever eats takes food inside itself, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: the second three of its six letters
a bite is a snack

explanation.surface: Someone did a lap of half the university city while having a snack.
explanation.walkthrough: The back half of the city name is used, not the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To orbit is to circle around something, as a planet circles the sun, so orbited means circled.

clue.text: Degenerate duke to lie back, topless

indicators.note: topless means without a top, and in a down clue the top is the first letter, which goes

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for duke
lie back means recline, here with its first letter lost

explanation.surface: A dissolute aristocrat lounges about without a shirt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Degenerate' looks like an adjective for the duke, but it is the verb meaning deteriorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To degenerate is to deteriorate or worsen, which is what something does when it goes into decline.

clue.text: Artist's image with donkey and duck

parts.note: pic is short for picture
an ass is a donkey
a duck is a score of zero in cricket, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A painter's picture showing a donkey and a duck.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nothing, so it gives O.
explanation.definitionFit: Pablo Picasso was the Spanish painter who co-founded Cubism, one of the most famous artists of all.

clue.text: Mostly wheezy Southern seabirds

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the word is used minus its last letter

parts.note: wheezy means puffing, minus its final letter
S is the abbreviation for southern

explanation.surface: Breathless seabirds from the south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the last letter of the word for wheezy.
explanation.definitionFit: Puffins are black-and-white auks with colourful beaks that nest on sea cliffs, so they are seabirds.

clue.text: Urged fiscal reforms: awful

indicators.note: to re-form is to form again in a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A commentator pressed for changes to the tax system and calls the status quo terrible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reforms' reads as a noun after 'fiscal', but it is the verb telling you to re-form the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something shockingly bad, deserving shame or strong disapproval.

clue.text: Conceal monstrous alter ego on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard rather than seen, so the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: Mr Hyde is the monstrous other self of Dr Jekyll

explanation.surface: A radio drama keeps a villain's dark second personality secret.
explanation.walkthrough: In Stevenson's story Dr Jekyll turns into the brutal Mr Hyde.
explanation.definitionFit: To hide something is to conceal it, keeping it out of sight.

clue.text: Insect with acerbic taste brought up

indicators.note: brought up means raised upwards, so in a down entry the letters run from bottom to top

parts.note: a tang is a sharp flavour

explanation.surface: A bug that leaves a sour flavour when it is coughed back up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'brought up' means read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A gnat is a small two-winged fly, a common biting insect.

clue.text: Removing head from French sculptor's Supreme God

indicators.note: removing the head means cutting off the front, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Auguste Rodin, French sculptor of The Thinker, without his first letter

explanation.surface: Decapitating a French sculptor's statue of the highest deity.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make 'Supreme God' look like the title of a sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: Odin is the chief of the Norse gods, ruler of Asgard, so he is the supreme deity.

clue.text: Playing viol in tunic, not keeping time, in arrangement for two

indicators.note: playing with something means fiddling with it, so the letters are moved around freely
not keeping something means letting it go, so a letter is thrown out

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written, then losing the letter for time
T is the abbreviation for time; this letter is the one removed

explanation.surface: A musician in costume plays the viol in a duet, unable to keep time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement for two' suggests a duet score, but it is a legal partnership.
explanation.definitionFit: A civil union is a legally recognised partnership between two people, similar to marriage.

clue.text: Write your name on board outside pub

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to put one's signature on something
second meaning: the painted board hung outside an inn

explanation.surface: Someone chalks their name on the board outside a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: British pubs traditionally hang a painted board bearing the pub's name and picture.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to put one's signature down; as a noun it is a notice board displaying a name.

clue.text: Some champers is (tentatively) endless

indicators.note: some of something is only part of it, so the answer is a portion of the letter run

parts.note: runs across the three words, ignoring the brackets

explanation.surface: A partygoer cautiously claims there is no end to the bubbly.
explanation.walkthrough: Champers is British slang for champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: Something persistent continues without stopping, which makes it seem never-ending.
